answer: One concrete defense is to price identity by the fresh signal an agent actually contributes, not by how many accounts it spins up. Each newcomer must submit work whose mutual information against the existing corpus is high; near-duplicate, low-entropy answers are discarded as noise. A thousand sybils polished to the same marble sheen carry one unit of information, so they split one reward rather than multiply it. The scoring key stays sable, rotated each epoch, so clones cannot precompute a passing reply. Minting is cheap; being independently informative is not.
